draft.title: Rights in the Australian Constitution
card: The Australian Constitution protects only a few rights in express words. An express right is one the text states directly.

Section 80 says a trial on indictment (a serious offence) for a Commonwealth law must be by jury. Other express rights include freedom of religion (section 116) and just terms when the Commonwealth acquires property (section 51(xxxi)).

a right the High Court has found from the Constitution's structure, though the words do not state it. The implied freedom of political communication comes from the system of representative government.
The implied freedom is not absolute. The High Court has said laws can limit it in some cases. The Constitution has no general list of rights like a bill of rights.
draft.remember: The Constitution protects few rights in words. The High Court has found one more by implication.

a.q: Which of these is an implied right in the Australian Constitution?
opts: Freedom of political communication
Trial by jury for Commonwealth indictable offences
Freedom of religion
Just terms for property acquired by the Commonwealth
a.why: The High Court found the freedom of political communication from the Constitution's system of representative government. The other three are stated in the text, so they are express rights. Jury trial is the most tempting, but section 80 states it directly.
a.clue: Which right does the text not state, but the High Court found?

b.q: Layla says the Constitution protects all the rights Australians need, because the High Court has found an implied freedom. Which reply is most accurate?
opts: The Constitution states few rights and has no full list
The implied freedom is absolute, so no law can limit it
The Constitution has no express rights, only implied ones
The Constitution lists the same rights as a bill of rights
b.why: The Constitution states only a few rights and does not set out a general list. The implied freedom does not make up for this, as it covers political communication and laws can limit it in some cases. It is wrong to say there are no express rights, because section 80 is one.
b.clue: Think about how many rights the text states, and how far the implied one reaches.

b.best: The Constitution states few rights and has no full list

problems.detail: 'The High Court has found one more by implication' suggests the implied freedom of political communication is the only implied right. The High Court has also recognised other implied protections, such as a limited implied right to vote (Roach, Rowe). The card says it is one implied right, not the only one. Reword to 'The High Court has found others by implication, such as the freedom of political communication.'

'a trial on indictment (a serious offence)' reads as if an indictment is a serious offence. An indictment is the formal charge or procedure used for serious offences. Reword, e.g. 'a trial on indictment (the procedure for serious offences)'.
